step1_analysis.description: The provided netlist represents the parasitic capacitance model of a MOSFET. In the context of the paper, this model is used to derive an analytical equation for the oscillation frequency of a ring oscillator by accounting for time-varying parasitics.

paper_reference.title: An Analytical Equation for the Oscillation Frequency of High-Frequency Ring Oscillators

oscillation_frequency.description: The fundamental frequency at which the ring oscillator toggles.

paper_reported.value: 8% (Note: This value from the abstract refers to the analytical model's average error, not the frequency itself)

sky130_expected.calculation: Period = 2 * N * td. For a 3-stage oscillator in SKY130 (L=0.15um), intrinsic td is ~20ps. With the added 5fF parasitic capacitors from the DUT loading the stages, td increases to ~50ps. Freq = 1 / (2 * 3 * 50ps) ~= 3.3 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Frequency is highly dependent on the assumed values for the parasitic capacitors and the sizing of the ring oscillator's driving transistors.

power_consumption.description: Average power drawn from the supply during steady-state oscillation.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = C_tot * VDD^2 * f. Estimated total switching capacitance C_tot ~= 50fF, VDD = 1.8V, f = 3.5GHz. P = 50e-15 * 3.24 * 3.5e9 = 567uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dynamic power dominates in ring oscillators and scales linearly with frequency and quadratically with supply voltage.

peak_to_peak_voltage.description: The maximum voltage swing of the oscillator nodes.

paper_reported.value: 500 mV (Likely a low-voltage supply test case mentioned in the paper)

sky130_expected.calculation: Standard CMOS ring oscillators swing rail-to-rail unless the frequency approaches the transit frequency (fT) of the technology.
sky130_expected.reasoning: At a 1.8V supply in SKY130, a 3.5 GHz oscillator will achieve nearly full rail-to-rail swing.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis of a 3-stage ring oscillator that incorporates the provided parasitic capacitance model as a load to measure oscillation frequency, power consumption, and voltage swing.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Ring Oscillator with Parasitic Model
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param VDD_VAL=1.8
Vdd VDD 0 {VDD_VAL}

* 3-stage ring oscillator
Xinv1 G D VDD 0 inv
Xinv2 D n3 VDD 0 inv
Xinv3 n3 G VDD 0 inv

.subckt inv in out vdd gnd
XMp out in vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=2u l=0.15u
XMn out in gnd gnd sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=1u l=0.15u
.ends

* Connect S and B to ground for the DUT
V_S S 0 0
V_B B 0 0

* DUT (Parasitic Capacitances - 5fF values added to make valid SPICE)
Cgs G S 5f
Cgd G D 5f
Cdb D B 5f
Cgb G B 5f
Csb S B 5f

* Initial conditions to kickstart oscillation
.ic v(G)=0 v(D)=1.8 v(n3)=0

.control
tran 5p 10n

* Measure Oscillation Frequency (using 10th and 11th cycles for steady state)
meas tran t1 trig v(G) val=0.9 rise=10 targ v(G) val=0.9 rise=11
let freq = 1 / t1
print freq

* Measure Power Consumption
meas tran pwr_avg avg i(Vdd) from=5n to=10n
let power = -pwr_avg * 1.8
print power

* Measure Peak-to-Peak Voltage
meas tran vmax max v(G) from=5n to=10n
meas tran vmin min v(G) from=5n to=10n
let vpp = vmax - vmin
print vpp

quit
.endc
.end
